script.problem: It has 2 sentences. Explanations are 3 to 5 sentences.

terra.problem: The text does not say Aeneas spent his mornings staring at the same ceiling.
The text says Peter visited the saints, but does not say they were present when he spoke to Aeneas.
“Mat and all” suggests Aeneas got up with his mat. The text says he got up, but does not say what he did with the mat.
The joke about Aeneas needing no lesson in “lying around” makes his paralysis and time bedridden the joke.
The text says Aeneas got up and people saw him. It does not say he was walking around.
“They send real people” makes the two men the senders. The disciples sent the two men to Peter.
The text does not say Dorcas used a needle and thread, or that sewing was how she did her works of kindness.
Tabitha opens her eyes in the same verse as Peter’s words, not the next verse.
The text says Tabitha saw Peter, but does not say he was the first person she saw.
The text does not say the widows were surprised or describe this as their best surprise.
The text does not state that the saints and widows loved Dorcas, or that all the saints mourned her.
Identifying Peter as Simon Peter connects two names not linked in this passage. The identification needs a verse that explicitly links them, such as Acts 10:5.
The claim that Levi appears in the Gospels is a Bible fact from outside the passage and needs a reference.
“Both crafts work with materials” is generic filler rather than a useful comparison or a line with Papa Dorin’s personality.
